claims.text: MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials are brittle in the as-cast or conventionally processed state.
MnNiSi-based materials exhibit a robust magnetocaloric response before the proposed treatment.
Warm forging or hot pressing near the magnetostructural transition temperature will refine the grain structure.
Warm forging or hot pressing near the magnetostructural transition temperature will introduce a controlled dislocation substructure.
The refined grains and controlled dislocation substructure will improve mechanical toughness.
The proposed thermomechanical treatment will preserve the large magnetocaloric effect.
For refrigeration applications, the relevant magnetic transition of the targeted MnNiSi-based materials is typically near room temperature.
Controlled deformation near the transition can produce microstructural changes without disturbing the magnetic phase transition.
An increased, controlled dislocation density relieves internal stresses and minimizes brittle failure modes.
Warm forging near the phase transition activates limited plastic deformation.
Grain refinement and dislocation engineering mitigate brittleness and enhance toughness.
A moderate post-deformation cooling regimen preserves the intrinsic magnetostructural coupling responsible for the magnetocaloric effect.
Warm-forged samples will have greater ductility and fracture toughness than untreated samples.
The magnetic entropy change and related magnetocaloric properties will remain essentially unchanged after warm forging.
Excessive processing temperature or deformation may cause unwanted phase changes or over-refinement that degrades magnetocaloric performance.
Heat treatment can alter magnetic homogeneity and magnetic functionality in magnetocaloric alloys.
